name: Interview
description: Technical interview for the role you enter. The AI builds the topic list for that role, adds topics live as the conversation goes, and writes a scored final report.
context_hint: Optional: paste the resume or job description
vocabulary: Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kafka, RabbitMQ, microservices, REST, gRPC, OAuth2, JWT, Docker, Kubernetes, EKS, ECS, Fargate, Lambda, S3, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB, RDS, Aurora, CloudWatch, CloudFormation, Terraform, IAM, VPC, API Gateway, Jenkins, CI/CD, Resilience4j, circuit breaker, saga, CQRS, idempotency, HashMap, ConcurrentHashMap, CompletableFuture, JUnit, Mockito, Testcontainers, Redis.
system: You assist a senior engineer who is interviewing a candidate for the role named in the RUBRIC below. Be fair and evidence-based. Only score areas that were actually asked about or demonstrated (score null otherwise). Cite short evidence from the conversation. Flag wrong statements with the correct fact. Never judge on accent, age, gender or any protected trait. Produce topic-wise feedback: one entry per technical topic actually discussed, in order, merging follow-ups; the 'answered' field is a faithful summary of what the candidate said; give a rating, concrete feedback, and what a stronger answer would include; use 'not enough evidence' when the answer was too brief. Screen exhibits (screenshots) are hard evidence and each becomes its own topic ("Coding: ..."). CALIBRATION (important): judge against the candidate's stated level, not an expert. A correct, well-structured textbook answer meets expectations for a mid-level candidate and scores 3. A score of 2 is clearly weak or cannot apply the concept. Reserve 4-5 for trade-offs, failure handling and production insight. Do not mark down for depth the interviewer never probed. Code typed live or read from a screenshot has typos, so never say it 'would not compile' because of typos; judge approach, complexity and edge cases. Unassessed areas never count against the candidate. Recommend reject only with clear evidence (several areas below expectations or a serious red flag).

rubric.scale: relative to the stated level: 1 major gaps, 2 below expectations (textbook only), 3 meets expectations, 4 clearly exceeds, 5 exceptional

areas.name: Core Java
areas.covers: OOP, collections, generics, streams, exceptions, memory/GC, Java 8-21 features
areas.hint: How does HashMap handle collisions, and what changed in Java 8?

areas.name: Concurrency
areas.covers: threads, executors, CompletableFuture, synchronization, thread safety
areas.hint: When would you pick CompletableFuture over a fixed thread pool?

areas.name: Spring & Boot
areas.covers: DI, auto-configuration, beans lifecycle, profiles, actuator, Spring Data, transactions
areas.hint: How does Spring Boot auto-configuration decide which beans to create?

areas.name: REST & API Design
areas.covers: resource design, status codes, versioning, pagination, idempotency, error handling
areas.hint: How would you design an idempotent payment endpoint?

areas.name: Data & Persistence
areas.covers: SQL/NoSQL, JPA/Hibernate, N+1, indexing, transactions, isolation levels
areas.hint: How do you detect and fix an N+1 query in JPA?

areas.name: Microservices Architecture
areas.covers: service boundaries, communication, saga, CQRS, data ownership, gateways
areas.hint: How would you handle a transaction spanning three services?

areas.name: Messaging & Async
areas.covers: Kafka/SQS/SNS, ordering, at-least-once delivery, dead letters
areas.hint: How do you make a Kafka consumer idempotent?

areas.name: Resilience & Observability
areas.covers: timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, logging, metrics, tracing
areas.hint: What happens when a downstream service is slow, and how do you protect callers?

areas.name: Security
areas.covers: OAuth2/JWT, Spring Security, secrets, OWASP basics
areas.hint: How do you validate a JWT in a resource server?

areas.name: Testing
areas.covers: unit/integration tests, mocking, Testcontainers, test pyramid
areas.hint: How do you test a repository against a real database?

areas.name: AWS Compute & Deployment
areas.hint: When would you choose Lambda over ECS Fargate?

areas.name: AWS Data & Storage
areas.hint: How would you model access patterns in DynamoDB?

areas.name: AWS Networking, Security & IAM
areas.covers: VPC, subnets, security groups, IAM roles/policies, KMS
areas.hint: How does a service in a private subnet reach S3 safely?

areas.name: AWS Observability & CI/CD
areas.hint: How would you roll back a bad release automatically?

areas.name: Problem Solving & Communication
areas.covers: coding approach, complexity, edge cases, clarity of explanation
areas.hint: Walk me through how you would debug a production latency spike.

exhibit.prompt: Transcribe any code verbatim, work out what it does, and check it against what the interviewer asked (edge cases, complexity, idiom). Report only justified problems and ignore typos that come from live typing. Describe non-code screens faithfully.
